mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.25% for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < previous year - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE > 5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 4% combined with a concurrent decline in CPIAUCSL below 2% signals a deep monetary easing and disinflation regime, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-on-month for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during triggered PAYEMS surges.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of more than 3% in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a synchronized collapse in demand channels, which strongly predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -3% AND HOUST monthly change < -3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between month-over-month changes in industrial production (INDPRO) and S&P 500 5-day forward returns: rising industrial production signals near-term positive equity returns due to improved earnings expectations.
failure_condition: The correlation between INDPRO monthly changes and S&P 500 5-day forward returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample tests.
